title: VeritySearch - Embedding + Rerank hosted API walkthrough
summary: Hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranker endpoints. Covered ingestion patterns, embedding vectors, candidate generation options (Elasticsearch + Pinecone), Redwood's rerank endpoint and tradeoffs (latency vs cost), security capabilities (SSO, KMS, audit logs), and next steps for a pilot and benchmark run.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Samir (Verity CTO), Lily (Lead ML Eng), Noah (Product), Ava (Infra)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Patel, I'm the AE working with VeritySearch. We're going to walk through our hosted embeddings and rerank flow and then leave time for Q&A. Ethan will drive the demo.
[00:12] Ethan (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick agenda: 1) ingestion & embed step, 2) candidate generation options, 3) reranker endpoint and scoring signals, 4) cost/latency tradeoffs and console tour.
[00:25] Samir (Verity CTO): Great, high level — our main goal is faster, more relevant results for enterprise search across docs and knowledge bases. Also data residency and audit trails are must-haves.
[00:38] Lily (Lead ML Eng): To be clear, right now we generate embeddings with our in-house pipeline and index in Elasticsearch but quality is inconsistent and we see drift when we update models. We're curious about switching to a hosted embed + rerank to simplify ops.
[00:55] Ethan: Makes sense. Quick qualification — what's your typical query volume?
[01:02] Noah (Product): Peak traffic is around 120 qps across our clusters, typical is 20-30 qps, and latency budget for search front-end is ~150ms for first pass and an extra 120ms for rerank ideally.
[01:18] Ava (Infra): Also compliance: we need SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and KMS for key management. SOC2 required for vendor.
[01:32] Maya: All standard asks. We have SOC2, SSO, audit export hooks to S3 and SIEM, and KMS/HSM integrations on Private deployments; hosted can support customer-managed keys via our partners. We'll attach the docs after the call.
[01:46] Ethan: Jumping into the demo — here's the Redwood Console. At the top left, model catalog, you can pick an embedding model. For hosted flow, the embed API call is a simple REST POST /v1/embeddings. Payload shows text batches. Example: we recommend 512-dimensional vectors for shorter docs; for long passages we chunk or use prefix caching.
[02:12] Ethan: One small note, our transcript auto labels K-V cache sometimes as 'K-V cash' in docs — ignore that, it's KV cache for the key/value attention cache.
[02:24] Lily: On embeddings: can we bring our model or must use Redwood-curated models?
[02:29] Ethan: For hosted, you use our catalog of verified open models. For Dedicated/Private you can either bring your model artifact or use a pinned catalog model. We can quantify latency/cost per model in the console.
[02:39] Samir: Candidate generation — we currently use Elasticsearch vector scoring. How would Redwood slot in?
[02:46] Ethan: Two common patterns: a) Candidate generation with your ES or Pinecone — just call /embed to produce vectors and put them into your index; call Redwood reranker with top K candidate ids + context; b) Use Redwood as both embed + store: we can host embedding store and provide a kNN candidate API. Most customers keep ES for metadata and use Redwood rerank to rescore.
[03:07] Noah: In pattern a), what's the overhead of sending top K to rerank?
[03:11] Ethan: Typically you pack the top 20-50 candidates and call /v1/rerank with the query, candidates, and optional signals. Rerank inference adds X ms — depends on model choice and KV cache hit rate. For our medium model expect ~80-120ms per rerank call on hosted standard tier, with batching can improve throughput if you accept a few extra ms.
[03:36] Lily: What's batching behavior? We don't want high tail latency spikes.
[03:40] Ethan: Our runtime does continuous batching with workload-aware policies. In the console you can set latency SLOs and aggressive batching if cost is priority. There are autoscaling knobs — default aims to keep p95 under configured SLO.
[03:55] Ava: About data residency — if we host embeddings with Redwood, can we restrict region?
[03:59] Maya: Yes, hosted regions are selectable; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll include region matrix in the doc pack.
[04:07] Ethan: Quick demo of rerank payload — you pass query text, candidate list (id, snippet, vector optional) and config like rerank_strategy: 'cross-encoder' or 'hybrid'. The response returns scores and an explain blob (short token highlights). Note: explain isn't full provenance, it's a model signal, not a deterministic rule.
[04:39] [00:04:40] Ethan continues: Real example — query: "How to reset enterprise SSO token"; candidates include docs A, B, C. Reranker bumps B to top because it matches troubleshooting steps.
[04:55] Samir: Can we attach external signals like click-through or time-on-doc?
[04:59] Ethan: Yes, you can pass signal fields in the candidate payload; we use that as additional features in the rerank model. There's also a simple weights config if you want TTL-style boosting.
[05:12] Lily: Any known gotchas on snippet length / tokenization between embed and rerank?
[05:17] Ethan: Make sure embedding chunking is consistent with what you send to rerank. We recommend storing both original doc and chunked embeddings; when you rerank, pass the exact snippet text you want scored. Mismatched tokenization can cause scoring drift — we've seen it with customers using different tokenizer versions.
[05:37] Maya: Let's cover cost numbers briefly. Hosted: per-embed + per-rerank request pricing. Dedicated gives lower per-token cost at the expense of committed capacity. We can show a cost simulation in the console.
[05:52] Noah: Do you have any benchmarking customers with similar qps and latency budgets?
[05:56] Ethan: Yes — one retailer with 100-150 qps used a hybrid: ES for quick pass and Redwood rerank for top 25, achieved p95 end-to-end ~210ms, cost reduced by 28% via prefix caching and quantized models. We'll share that benchmark sheet.
[06:15] Samir: Security — specifically SSO and audit logs. How granular are audit logs?
[06:21] Maya: We provide token-level usage logs, API keys usage, and per-route traces. For Private deployments we can ship logs to your SIEM; hosted supports log export to S3 and direct syslog integration for enterprise tiers.
[06:34] Ava: KMS — customer-managed keys?
[06:36] Ethan: On Dedicated/Private, yes. On hosted we offer bring-your-own-key via partner integrations; some customers prefer Dedicated when they require HSM-backed keys.
[06:48] Lily: About model updates: We want to pin a model version for stable behavior. How do rollouts work?
[06:54] Ethan: Console supports model pinning and canary rollouts per route. You can set traffic split and automatic rollback on quality regressions if you feed eval sets. Our Optimize product can run quality checks against your prompt set and surface regressions.
[07:10] [00:07:10] Ethan: Now a quick live run — I'm uploading a small sample doc set and running an embed job. Watch the job show per-batch progress and estimated cost.
[07:23] [00:07:23] Ethan: Job completed — vector store shows 5,000 docs ingested. Now I'm running a query via the demo client: topK from ES then rerank.
[07:35] [00:07:35] Ethan: Query time — vector search ~45ms, rerank call ~95ms, total ~140ms for this test. That's within their target.
[07:45] Noah: Nice, though our real payload might have heavier text.
[07:49] Ethan: Right, longer snippets increase token counts. We recommend truncation strategies and passing only the most relevant snippet to rerank. Prefix caching can help for repeated prefixes.
[08:01] Lily: Talk about embeddings dimensionality — will changing vector dims break our index?
[08:05] Ethan: Changing dims requires reindexing; we usually recommend sticking to a stable dimension in production. Optimize can recommend quantization to shrink footprint without reindexing.
[08:18] Maya: Any objections on hosted vs dedicated? Samir?
[08:22] Samir: Hosted looks quick to get started, but our compliance team leans Dedicated for KMS/HSM and residency. Also curious on cold-start behavior and p95 spikes.
[08:33] Ethan: Cold start is mitigated by warm pools and steady-state autoscaling; p95 spikes often come from tail requests with big token counts — we can set per-request limits or fallback to a cheaper model.
[08:46] Ava: What about rate limiting and quotas we can enforce per-team?
[08:50] Maya: Console supports per-token and per-route quotas as well as token-level cost visibility. You can attach policies to API keys or SSO groups.
[08:59] Lily: For the reranker model, can we do custom fine-tune on our clicks?
[09:03] Ethan: Short answer: yes, on Dedicated/Private you can fine-tune or host a fine-tuned variant; on hosted we provide curated model variants and a steering mechanism via prompts and feature signals. We'll outline options in the follow-up.
[09:17] [00:09:17] Ethan: Quick peek at Optimize — here we have a prompt eval suite. You can upload labeled query sets, run A/B between model versions, and see MRR/Recall deltas. It integrates with the console rollouts.
[09:32] Noah: Good. For pilot success, our metrics would be: 1) +12% MRR on internal queries, 2) end-to-end p95 under 300ms, 3) clear ops cut (reduce indexing complexity).
[09:45] Maya: That's a solid framing for an initial pilot. We'll propose a 6-week pilot: weeks 1-2 data prep & ingest, week 3 run benchmarks, week 4 optimize rerank prompts, week 5 canary, week 6 wrap and ROI review.
[09:58] Samir: Timeline-wise, compliance review will take 2-3 weeks — so pilot start late November/early December sounds plausible.
[10:06] Ethan: On benchmarking, we'll run an A/B against your current ES-only pipeline and provide the eval harness. We'll need 5k-10k queries, and a small label set for quality checks.
[10:16] Lily: We'll prepare that. Also, can we test private data without exposing to hosted? We're comfortable sharing sanitized subsets.
[10:22] Maya: That's fine — many customers run initial pilots with sanitized or hashed data. For deeper tests we can set up Dedicated trial nodes.
[10:32] [00:10:32] Ethan: Moving to Q&A — any other deep technical concerns?
[10:36] Noah: Operationally, how do we handle rollback if rerank changes degrade metrics?
[10:40] Ethan: Canary rollouts and instant rollbacks are built into the console; Optimize can trigger automatic rollback based on your eval thresholds. Also we keep model snapshots.
[10:51] Lily: How deterministic is rerank? If two calls have same payload will scores be identical?
[10:56] Ethan: Generally yes but there can be nondeterminism from model sampling or floating point artifacts across hardware. We provide seeds for deterministic runs on Dedicated.
[11:06] Samir: About logs — do we store request payloads?
[11:09] Maya: By default we store minimal metadata; we can enable payload logging for enterprise with retention controls. It's configurable to meet privacy needs.
[11:20] Ava: Are there examples of customers that transitioned off ES into a Redwood-hosted datastore?
[11:24] Ethan: A couple in healthcare moved embeddings to Redwood for performance and used ES for metadata. We can share anonymized case studies.
[11:34] Noah: Any resource docs we can look at?
[11:36] Maya: We'll send a doc pack: security pack, region matrix, pilot playbook, and a cost simulation exported from the console.
[11:44] Samir: Sounds good. Last question — can we get a quick price estimate for 100 qps baseline and 120 qps peaks?
[11:50] Maya: We'll include a simulation with hosted and dedicated options. Quick gut: hosted for pilot likely cheaper short-term; Dedicated wins at 24/7 heavy usage.
[12:02] Ethan: Wrapping up — I'll attach the rerank prompt examples and the eval harness. We'll also include a sample API client and a Postman collection.
[12:12] Maya: Thanks everyone. Quick recap of next steps: Maya sends pricing & security, Ethan shares benchmark harness and prompts, Lily uploads sample docs. We'll schedule POC scoping next week.
[12:24] Samir: Appreciate the walkthrough, excited to try the pilot.
[12:28] Noah: Thanks team.
[12:30] [END]
